label: High at D2 when S2 is reached; previous reward raises it at D1, lowers at D2; high at GO after S2.
short_terms: (phase == D2) * (state == S2) ;; (phase == D1) * prev_reward - (phase == D2) * prev_reward ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0)
terms: (phase == D2) * (state == S2) ;; (phase == D1) * prev_reward ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == GO) * prev_reward ;; (phase == D2) * prev_reward ;; (phase == GO) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * prev_reward ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S2) * prev_reward
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 21. Dominant driver is the state just shown at D2: about +0.13 when S2 is reached vs S1 (the this choice x state table alone gives 0.71 beyond timing), independent of the choice that led there. The previous trial reward (the reward input at D1) raises it at D1 (~+0.06) and, signed oppositely, lowers it at D2 of the same trial; at GO it is higher when the previous trial reached S2 (~+0.05, a carried-over trace of the D2 state). Belief log-odds adds almost nothing once these are included. The free fit (dev 0.73 vs short 0.71) adds a smaller GO reward effect (unrewarded trials raise GO), a state x reward interaction at D2, and a small trial-before reward term. All terms are observed; no future variables used.

issues: The GO claim ('high at GO after S2') is mostly wrong. Scored alone, (phase == GO) * (prev_state == S2) explains only 0.004 test R^2 beyond timing, against 0.060 for (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0). The residual table agrees: GO residuals run from +0.017 to +0.069 after unrewarded trials and from -0.042 to +0.014 after rewarded ones, for both states.

Replacing the GO term with (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.707 to 0.816 (dev 0.816; weight +0.078). That beats the agent's own free fit (0.73). The prev_state term was standing in, badly, for the reward effect at GO.

Misses on the recorded short form show a large systematic error at GO after unrewarded trials. It under-predicts GO after a1 S1 u by +0.076, after a1 S2 u by +0.060 and after a2 S1 u by +0.049. In the worst windows GO is about 0.24 actual against about 0.10 predicted, after r0.

Using prev_reward directly at GO fails (weight about 0, R^2 0.655) because prev_reward is not purely 0/1 (it is 0 on an episode's first trial and can be -1). The binary (prev_reward == 0) form is the one that works; (prev_reward != 1) scores the same.
The D2-state term (+0.15) and the shared D1-up / D2-down reward term (+0.057) do hold up. Dropping the GO term entirely leaves 0.654.

With the corrected form the remaining misses are smaller: D1 and GO after a1 S2 r are about +0.05, and D2 after S2-unrewarded trials is about -0.04. These are modest, and no large error class remains.
